{"outcome":"DIRECT_SUB_OPTIMAL","best_model_id":"PGS000549","confidence":"Moderate","rationale":"Endpoint match: target is ovarian neoplasm; among candidates, the PRSweb models (PGS000544–PGS000564) explicitly use trait_efo=ovarian neoplasm and phenotyping_reported="Malignant neoplasm of ovary", which is the closest direct endpoint alignment per the trait-label guidance (read_skill_section("trait_labels")). Many other candidates are ovarian carcinoma/epithelial ovarian cancer or restricted subgroups (e.g., BRCA carriers), which are less faithful to a generic ovarian neoplasm target.

Performance evidence: most candidates only report full-model AUROC/C-index (not PRS-only), which is not ideal for cross-model ranking; within the ovarian-neoplasm-matched PRSweb set, PGS000549 has the strongest reported discrimination and PRS contribution (full-model AUROC 0.567 with Nagelkerke pseudo-R² 0.00996) compared with the other ovarian-neoplasm PRSweb alternatives (generally AUROC ~0.52–0.56 and lower pseudo-R²). This follows the performance-metrics guidance that, absent PRS-only metrics, we can still use within-family comparable full-model metrics and R²-like summaries cautiously (read_skill_section("performance_metrics")).

Heritability sanity check: a direct EUR heritability record for "ovarian neoplasm" was not found; a broader lookup for "ovarian cancer" returned only weakly related ovarian-condition records (e.g., ovarian cyst/PCOS) rather than ovarian malignancy, so h2 cannot strongly calibrate expectations here (get_heritability_records). Given the modest pseudo-R² values, nothing appears implausibly high.

Why sub-optimal: even the best ovarian-neoplasm-matched candidate shows only modest discrimination and lacks PRS-only AUROC/R²; several higher-AUROC models exist (e.g., PGS003385) but are for ovarian serous carcinoma (subtype) rather than ovarian neoplasm broadly, so they are not preferred for this target."}
